The value is taken directly from user-controlled CSV content with no validation against Enrollment.STATUS_CHOICES (pending/active/completed/dropped). SINK: Enrollment.objects.update_or_create(..., defaults={"status": status}) at line 586 writes the raw CSV status to the database. An admin uploading a crafted CSV can set any arbitrary status string, including invalid values or values that bypass normal enrollment workflow logic (e.g., setting 'completed' on newly imported enrollments).

extra.message: CSV Import File Type Validated by Extension Only

metadata.proof: SOURCE: ImportUploadForm.clean_csv_file (line 179) receives the uploaded file and only checks file.name.lower().endswith(".csv") at line 181. No content-type verification, magic-byte sniffing, or MIME validation is performed. SINK: The validated file is returned and processed by the import_enrollments view (views.py:573-574) with csv.DictReader. An attacker can rename any file (e.g., an executable, script, or large binary) to .csv and the server will accept it, attempting to parse it as CSV. While csv.DictReader will likely produce errors on non-CSV content, the lack of content validation allows resource exhaustion or parser-behavior exploitation with malformed CSV structures.
